utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So much for a slow August.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Gail is saying we have a lot of interns.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So welcome interns.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Oh, no, don't get us in trouble for saying what is upstate and not upstate.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Okay, I just want to thank everyone for being here, and I want to thank my colleagues who are here, Council

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Member Shahana Hanif, Council Member Lincoln Ressler, Council Member Shanel Thomas-Henry, Council Member Gail Brewer, Council Member Frank Morano, Council Member Mercedes Narcisse, Council Member Harvey Epstein, Council Member Oswald Feliz.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We have a lot of legislation, a lot going on, so really appreciate everyone being here today.

chapters.summary: Menin shares historic news that City Council employee Rafael Rubio, wrongfully detained by ICE in January, has been granted permanent asylum and returned to work at the Council after a long legal battle.
chapters.title: Menin announces Rafael Rubio granted permanent asylum

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So I want to start off with just incredible news that we received this week, and that is that our city council employee, Rafael Rubio, has been granted permanent asylum.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: This is historic.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: This was a very long battle.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: As you all know, he was wrongfully detained by ICE in January.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We were heavily involved in his legal case, getting him legal counsel to file habeas petition, getting him new legal counsel later on that he needed.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And I could not be more overjoyed that he is back home in New York City where he belongs and he's back working at the New York City Council.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So this is really just incredible news because this fight has now finally come to an end.

chapters.summary: Menin condemns the Trump administration's decision to end TPS for Haitian immigrants, stripping work permits and risking deportation, and expresses solidarity with Haitian council members Narcisse, Joseph, Lewis, and Ossé.
chapters.title: Menin addresses TPS termination for Haitian immigrants

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: But tragically, the fate of so many other New Yorkers who have been taken by ICE have not been so fortunate.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: The federal government continues to inflict harm on our immigrant communities, and Haitian New Yorkers are its latest victims.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Last week, the Trump administration announced that they would be ending TPS for Haitian immigrants, stripping them of their work permits and leaving them vulnerable to deportation.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: This is a tremendous injustice, not only for those whose livelihoods are in limbo, but for their families and for our entire city that relies on their countless contributions.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: The council stands in solidarity with council members Mercedes Narcisse, Councilmember Rita Joseph, Councilmember Farah Lewis, Councilmember Chi-A.-Ossé,

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: who all represent the very best of our Haitian New York community and who are mobilizing to assist our Haitian neighbors through

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: legal access, and know your rights campaigns.

chapters.summary: Menin addresses the expiration of federal funding for unaccompanied minor legal aid, praises Governor Hochul's $7 million state commitment, and highlights the Council's $82 million budget allocation for immigration legal services.
chapters.title: Menin discusses funding for immigrant children's legal services

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: The administration is also abandoning our most vulnerable immigrants, our children, having let federal funding for legal aid expire at the end of July.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: But New York is not sitting idly by.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Yesterday, Governor Hochul announced that the state will provide more than $7 million to legal aid services supporting unaccompanied minors, and I applaud her for the action she's taking.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And I also want to mention the funding, approximately $82 million of funding the city council pushed for and we received in the budget for legal immigration services.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And that is something that we will absolutely continue to fund moving forward.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Every person has a right to representation, including and particularly a scared child without their parents.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: It's simply unconscionable to think otherwise.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: The governor's commitment, as I mentioned, also boasters his council's funding that supports various legal agencies that work with immigrants.

chapters.summary: Menin announces the Council is launching a legislative inquiry into Kalshi, Polymarket, Coinbase, and Gemini for potentially deceptive advertising practices targeting minors in online betting, citing her experience as a mother and former Consumer Affairs Commissioner.
chapters.title: Menin announces investigation into prediction market platforms targeting minors

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: From City Hall to Albany, New York continues to stand by our immigrant neighbors, and we are always a resource for all people in need.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Another avenue we're pursuing to protect our New Yorkers revolves around predatory marketing practices.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So I was really proud yesterday to announce that the City Council is beginning an investigation into four different platforms.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Kalshi, Polymarket, Coinbase.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: and Gemini, and we notified them of the investigation.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We are conducting a legislative inquiry.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: What we're really looking at is we're looking at the practices that we believe are targeting minors, that are luring minors into this online betting.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And so we asked, we sent a long letter.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: If anyone is interested in receiving a copy, please talk to Jack.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: But we really believe that the next generation of New Yorkers is increasingly being targeted by prediction market industries, aggressive and what we believe potentially deceptive advertising practices.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So our goal in this investigation is to determine whether additional laws, funding, or programs, or all of the above are needed to protect them if the allegations indeed prove to be true.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And I say this as both a mother and as a former commissioner of the Department of Consumer Affairs.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We take these consumer protection issues incredibly seriously.

chapters.summary: Menin introduces the SCOOP Act, a package of bills to expand access to dog waste bags, launch a composting pilot at dog runs, establish a public education campaign, and strengthen enforcement, noting over 2,000 dog waste complaints this year.
chapters.title: Menin introduces SCOOP Act dog waste legislation package

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Not only do we have the ability, but we have an obligation to harness the full weight of this city council to protect minors from practices that appear to be aimed at them.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Shifting gears onto potentially a lighter note, I want to talk about today's legislation.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We are so excited to pass the bills from the SCOOP Act.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: This package of bills will expand access to dog waste bags.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: It will also launch a pilot program to compost waste elected from dog runs.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: It is...

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: establishes a public education campaign, and it strengthens enforcement of these rules.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: This is about creating a safer, cleaner environment in communities all across New York City.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Look, there were over 2,000 complaints about dog waste just this year alone.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: This is an increasing problem, and so the council is now acting to address it.

chapters.summary: Menin highlights rising insurance costs across NYC—small businesses paying 4-5x more, homeowners 26% more, auto insurance 42% above national average—and introduces legislation creating the nation's first Office of Insurance Affordability with claim adjusters to help consumers.
chapters.title: Menin discusses insurance affordability crisis and new accountability office

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Another factor that is affecting New York is obviously the affordability crisis, and particularly one factor driving this crisis is rising insurance costs, costs that are some of the highest in the country.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So, for example, if you're a small business owner, you will be paying, on average, four to five times more on your liability insurance than if you were a small business in another state.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: If you're a homeowner in New York City, on average, you're going to be paying 26% more than homeowners in other areas.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: If health care costs, obviously the same thing.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: If you drive a car in New York City, your insurance is 42% higher than the national average.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So with this bill that we are passing today, it creates the nation's first insurance accountability office to bring transparency around insurance costs, to drive the cost down.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We're also going to have claim adjusters that are on staff that are going to help New Yorkers navigate this maze and bureaucracy around rising insurance costs.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And I do want to just say that the city lost 8,000 businesses in the second quarter of 2025 alone.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So one of the rising costs for small businesses that we're hearing time and time again is high cost of insurance.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And so that is one of the many reasons that we are tackling this.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And this new office is going to engage insurers, stakeholders, and regulators to really address this.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Key issue that is affecting affordability in our city.

chapters.summary: Menin previews the outdoor dining bills allowing year-round operation, addressing quality of life concerns including sanitation and noise, setting an 11 p.m. closing time, and establishing penalties for non-compliant restaurant owners.
chapters.title: Menin introduces outdoor dining legislation package

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: As the summer comes to a close, I'm sure the last thing that we want on our minds is the winter months, but restaurant owners are always looking ahead and we in the council are looking out for them.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: After passing a package of bills on outdoor dining that we're going to be doing today, sidewalk cafes can operate 365 days a year and for many restaurants the ability to serve customers outside all year round provides vital revenue.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: As a former restaurant owner myself, I know how important this is to make sure that outdoor dining is year-round because it's really a lifeline to these restaurants.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: At the same time, we want to ensure that our neighbors are as satisfied as our restaurant owners and diners, and that's exactly why some of the bills in this package are going to be addressing quality of life issues, sanitation issues,

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: rats, and other quality of life issues that we heard about the outdoor dining program.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So one of the bills, and each member will be talking about

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Their bills, but one of the bills establishes penalties for restaurant owners who do not properly clean the site.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Another sets an end time in the evenings at 11 p.m.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So whether you live in the restaurant's neighborhood or you're just there for a meal, our outdoor dining plan hopes to make all New Yorkers happy.

chapters.summary: Menin lists land use items up for vote including rezonings in Queens and a park site selection, finance items including the transparency resolution and ECB intro, and resolutions on James Baldwin Day, insurance costs, and the Staten Island flag.
chapters.title: Menin outlines stated agenda: land use, finance, and legislation items

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So now we're going to move on to our stated agenda.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: First, we'll be voting on the following land use items.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: 50-20 108th Street rezoning, which facilitates the development of two new mixed-use buildings in Councilmember Thomas Henry's district.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: 63-02 Fresh Pond Road rezoning will enable the development of a new seven-story mixed-use building in Councilmember Wong's district.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Queen CD2 Walk to the Park site selection will facilitate the creation of new parkland in the districts of Council Members Krishnan and Wan.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Flatiron Nomad Major Concessions will approve the expansion of the existing Flatiron District concession area boundaries in the districts of Council Members Wilson and Epstein.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And next, we're going to vote on the following finance items, a transparency resolution approving new designations and changes of certain organizations receiving funding in the expense budget.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: A pre-considered introduction sponsored by Councilmember Linda Lee would require the Department of Finance Commissioner to establish a temporary program to resolve outstanding ECB judgment.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: penalties.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Today we're also going to vote on the following pieces of legislation.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We have a lot, so bear with me.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Resolution 218, sponsored by Councilmember Crystal Hudson, would declare August 2nd annually as James Baldwin Day in the City of New York to honor his legacy as a groundbreaking essayist,

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: novelist, playwright, poet, and civil rights activist.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Resolution 395, sponsored by Councilmember Frank Marano, would call on Albany to sign legislation prohibiting increases in rates of homeowners insurance in excess of 25% per year.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Resolution 389, sponsored by Councilmember Eric Dinowitz, would call on Albany to sign the Automobile Insurance Consumer Information Act.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Resolution 387, sponsored by Councilmember Gail Brewer, would call on Albany to sign legislation to mitigate the rising cost of property insurance for affordable housing.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Important issue we were just talking about.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Introduction 320-A, sponsored by Councilmember Frank Marano, would codify into law the current flag of the borough of Staten Island as an official flag.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And you're standing like right there, right over there.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Perfect.

chapters.summary: Council Member Frank Morano celebrates his first major legislation, codifying the Staten Island flag as NYC's third official flag, arguing it signals to Staten Islanders that the city sees and values them, and praising Speaker Menin as the best speaker Staten Island has had.
chapters.title: Morano speaks on codifying Staten Island flag as official city flag

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And now I invite Councilmember Marano to the podium to discuss his legislation.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you, Speaker, for the opportunity and for your courage.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: It does take a lot of courage, as anybody that knows me can tell you, to hand me a microphone without the timer that automatically starts buzzing after two minutes.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: But in all seriousness, this is the first opportunity I've had to participate in a pre-stated meeting press conference because this is the first

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: major piece of legislation that I've been able to pass since joining the council last year.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And I'm very excited about it.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I'm excited about it, even though it's heavy on symbolism and doesn't necessarily change the cost of living for a lot of Staten Islanders.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: It doesn't necessarily change what time they have to go up or the length of their commute time.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: But the truth is, for two generations, maybe more, Staten Islanders have felt forgotten by the city.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: They have felt alienated from New York City government.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: They feel as if city government doesn't speak for them.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And they feel, quite frankly, in many instances, unrepresented.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And what we're doing today in codifying that Staten Island flag and making it the third official flag of New York City behind Brooklyn and the boogie down Bronx

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: is a major step in telling Staten Islanders that the city of New York sees you and wants you to be a part of city government.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: So often, Staten Islanders that I meet who are flying the American flag, they don't seem to have that same sense of pride and patriotism in their city and their borough.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Every day, I am meeting Staten Islanders.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Islanders who seem to be counting the days until they can retire and move to Florida, North Carolina, Arizona, New Jersey, wherever.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I want this flag flown all over Staten Island with the same pride that the American flag is on Flag Day and on the 4th of July.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And I think making it official and having our city government say that Staten Island counts is a big first step.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: This is done totally in a nonpartisan fashion.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: All three members of Staten Island City Council delegation fought for this every step of the way.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And I really can't thank Speaker Menon enough for her leadership, not just on this issue, but on being the best speaker Staten Island has ever had.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Last year, you know how many Staten Islanders were chairing committees or in the leadership of the city council?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Zero.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And now all three of us are in the leadership of the council or chairing committees.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: That's no small thing.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Beyond that, we've had the largest investment of capital money in Staten Island under Speaker Menon's leadership that we've seen in decades.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: So it's nice for the first time that now not only do we have a speaker that says Staten Island is part of this city, but actually works and hears the needs of Staten Islanders.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And that's not to say anything about her leadership in stopping property taxes and fighting against police cuts.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: So I'm very excited that from now on, when you see this flag all over our...

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: It will now be official.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And it's upside down.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: When you see this flag.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: A big shout out.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: We're going to turn it around.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: A big shout out.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: There you go.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: There you go.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: A big shout out to former borough president Jimmy Otto, who commissioned this flag 10 years ago, and to Emil Micah, who designed this flag.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: He's Staten Island's own Betsy Ross.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: So thank you.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you, Speaker.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: You know what?

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I don't know how we're going to match that.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We're really not.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: You know what?

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: The next time you pass a bill, we're not putting you first.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Not fair to the other council members.

chapters.summary: Menin introduces Intro 935A by Council Member Feliz, requiring NYPD to report weekly on confirmed firearm discharges including date, time, location, and circumstances.
chapters.title: Menin introduces Feliz's firearm discharge reporting bill

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I also want to mention we've been joined by our majority whip, Camilla Hanks, and Councilmember Pierina Sanchez.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So now, introduction 935A, sponsored by Councilmember Oswald-Feliz, would require the NYPD to report on the number of confirmed firearm discharges in the city on a weekly basis.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: The NYPD would be required to report the date.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: The time, the location of each firearm discharge, as well as a description of the circumstances of the discharge.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And I now want to invite the council member to the podium to discuss his legislation.

chapters.summary: Council Member Feliz explains his bill addresses a gap in NYPD data, which only tracks shootings where someone is struck, not all discharges. He argues shots fired data is essential for a complete picture of gun violence and resource allocation.
chapters.title: Feliz speaks on shots fired data reporting bill

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: I am definitely not going to be able to match that, but I'll try my best.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: I'm New York City Councilmember Oswald Feliz, proudly representing the Bronx.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: and the chair of the Public Safety Committee.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: So thankful and grateful that we're passing my shots fired bill today.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Public safety is one of the most important duties of city government.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: And it is important that the picture that we provide or the picture that our crime-related data provides, it's important that that picture be full and clear.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Now, and this is especially true on the issue of gun violence.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Now, as we know, the NYPD provides a lot of data related to gun violence, including shooting victims and also shooting incidents.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: But the data related to shooting incidents only includes data of shooting incidents when someone is struck.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: It doesn't include incidents where there's a shooting, for example, and no one is struck.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: These incidents are serious, and lack of data on them has prevented us from being able to see a full and clear picture on the issue of gun violence in the city of New York.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: That shot fire data is essential.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Again, it helps us provide a full and clear picture on the issue of gun violence in the city of New York.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: It also allows us to be able to better track the progress that we're making on that issue.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: And it also helps us be able to determine what parts of the city need additional resources.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: So this legislation will help us do exactly that.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: By requiring data on shots fired incidents, including data related to the date, location, the borough, the precinct, and the time.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: And I just want to thank our wonderful speaker, Julie-Menin, for making this bill and also making public safety in general a top priority.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: I also want to thank my co-prime sponsor, Joann-Ariola.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Councilmember.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: It's a very important bill for public safety, so thank you so much for your leadership on that.

chapters.summary: Menin introduces Intro 839A by Council Member Pierina Sanchez, making the certification of no harassment pilot program permanent.
chapters.title: Menin introduces Sanchez's certification of no harassment bill

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Introduction 839A, sponsored by Councilmember Pierina-Sanchez, will make the certification of no harassment pilot program permanent.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And now I want to invite Councilmember Sanchez to talk about her bill.

chapters.summary: Sanchez explains the bill makes CONH permanent, expands the harassment definition to include ICE threats, monitors problematic landlord portfolios, creates stronger incentives to clear violations, and clarifies that basic maintenance remains allowed under the program.
chapters.title: Sanchez speaks on making CONH program permanent and stronger

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Do the stanky leg.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Very, very excited.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Speaker, and thank you to my 30 colleagues who have signed on as co-sponsors to this legislation.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And I'm just going to take a moment of privilege to thank Ben Ratner from our team, Deputy Chief of Staff for Policy, who has treated this as his legislative baby.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: The legislative baby will be born today after the vote.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: So, look, every tenant in New York City deserves to live free of harassment, regardless of their citizenship status.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: In New York City, it's already unlawful for landlords to retaliate against any tenant who's exercising their rights as a tenant.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: For instance, if they're suffering from a rat infestation and they call 311, it is unlawful for that landlord to call to harass that tenant and retaliate.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: However, we are seeing rising instances of harassment, and specifically we're at a time where the federal government is targeting immigrant communities, and we have to ensure that all of our neighbors are receiving the strongest possible tenant protection.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: So that's why today the council is voting on 839A, legislation that will make the certification of no harassment program permanent and stronger.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: The CONH program was first created in 2018 to deter owners from using construction as harassment.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And from displacing tenants from their home.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: After two successful pilots, the CONH has proven itself useful for identifying high-risk buildings and deterring bad actors from bad behavior.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: So today we're building on that success and codifying CONH as a permanent tool in the city's enforcement toolkit.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Specifically, the program is changing to respond to rising reports of landlords threatening to call ICE on their tenants by expanding the definition of harassment.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Second, we're going to be monitoring problematic portfolios by reviewing all buildings that have the same owner to those with a finding of harassment.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And third, we're creating stronger incentives to clear violations by allowing buildings to exit the program only if owners significantly improve building conditions for their tenants.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Finally, this bill is clarifying that basic maintenance continues to be allowed.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Y'all, basic maintenance is allowed.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: The CONH program for the buildings that are within the program does not disallow basic repairs.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: That has been some misinformation that has been out there.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: I want to take a moment to really address it.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And then just to close, I want to thank all of my colleagues, the Coalition of Advocates, and especially ANHD, who have long championed this program.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And going forward, I'm going to be talking about the program.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: I'm looking forward to working with the administration, with HPD, to steward this program to its best version possible.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you, Speaker.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

chapters.summary: Menin introduces Intro 872 by Council Member Hanif, requiring DOHMH and Sanitation to develop a multilingual public education campaign on dog waste removal.
chapters.title: Menin introduces Hanif's dog waste education bill

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Introduction 872, and now we're moving into the SCOOP Act.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Introduction 872, sponsored by Councilmember Shahana Hanif, would require the Commissioner of DOHMH in consultation with the Commissioner of Sanitation to develop and conduct a public education

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: and outreach campaign to inform the public about dog waste removal and the dangers of failing to remove dog waste.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So inviting Councilmember Hanif to talk about her bill.

chapters.summary: Hanif details the public health and environmental hazards of dog waste, citing EPA and CDC data on waterway pollution and bacteria, and explains her bill includes effectiveness evaluation using 311 data to measure progress.
chapters.title: Hanif speaks on citywide dog waste education campaign

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Hi, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: I'm Councilmember Shahana Hanif.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: I chair the Disabilities Committee.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: I am thrilled that today the Council will be passing

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Intro 872A, my legislation creating a citywide multilingual dog waste education campaign.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Thank you to Speaker Menon, my colleagues on the council, and the advocates who worked alongside us to make this legislation part of the SCOOP Act package and to pass that package today.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Let me just first start by saying I love dogs.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: We all know New York City has a dog poop problem.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: We've seen it, we've smelled it, and unfortunately, many of us have stepped in it.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: But this is more about an unpleasant sidewalk experience.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Dog waste is a serious public health hazard and environmental hazard.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: According to the EPA and CDC, pet waste can pollute our waterways and spread harmful bacteria and parasites, including E.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Coli, salmonella, and roundworm.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: And while many New Yorkers know they're supposed to pick up after their dogs, not everyone understands the public health consequences when they don't.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: That's why this bill takes an important step, educating New Yorkers about why picking up after our pets matters

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: and their legal obligation to do so, and making sure that information is accessible in multiple languages.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: And importantly, this legislation will also help us understand whether the campaign is actually working.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: This bill...

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: includes a report evaluating its effectiveness and incorporates 311 data on reports and sightings of dog waste.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: That means we'll have real data to help us measure progress and identify where additional education may be needed.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: This is what effective city government should look like, addressing a problem New Yorkers experience every single day, investing in education and using data to make sure our solutions are actually working.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Every New Yorker deserves sidewalks that are clean, safe, and accessible, and every dog guardian owner has a role to play in keeping our neighborhoods that way.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Thank you again, and I'm thrilled to be passing this legislation today.

chapters.summary: Menin introduces Intro 864 by Council Member Epstein, requiring Parks to establish a pilot program collecting dog waste from dog runs for composting.
chapters.title: Menin introduces Epstein's dog waste composting pilot bill

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And also part of the SCOOP Act is Introduction 864, sponsored by Councilmember Harvey Epstein.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: This bill would require the Commissioner of Parks to establish a pilot program to collect dog waste from dog runs under the Department of Parks jurisdiction for composting.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So Councilmember Epstein.
